from datetime import datetime
_l=lab
def lab2(q):
    s=q.lower()
    if re.search(r'what year|in what year|quantity|\bfare\b|how much|what is the (second |highest |lowest )?(highest|lowest|largest)? ?(speed|cost|price)',s) and not re.search('stand for',s): return 'num'
    if re.search(r'second highest mountain|what is the full name',s): return 'ent'
    return _l(q)
D=collections.defaultdict(list)
for d,u,q in rows: D[u].append((datetime.strptime(d,'%b %d, %Y'),lab2(q)))
cut=datetime(2023,2,1)
ok={}
for u,v in D.items():
    has=any(l in('desc','num') for _,l in v)
    good=all(d>cut for d,l in v if l=='num')
    ok[u]=has and good
us=sorted(u for u in ok if ok[u],key=int)
res=[f"({a}, {b})" for i,a in enumerate(us) for b in us[i+1:]]
print(len(us),len(res))
open('/work/answer.txt','w').write('\n'.join(res) if res else '[]')

I wrote 5,778 pairs to `/work/answer.txt`, but the labels behind them are approximate, so some pairs may be wrong.

The file has no labels, so I assigned each of the 787 questions a label with keyword rules (for example, "How many" became numeric value and "Who" became human being). I spot-checked a sample of about 40 and saw several likely mislabels, such as "What county is Chicago in ?" labelled as entity. I patched a few rules, like "What year" and "fare" going to numeric value. I did not check every question.

A user qualified if they had at least one description and abstract concept or numeric value question. They also needed every numeric value question dated after February 1, 2023. A user with no numeric value questions passes that second test automatically. That gave 108 qualifying users. The answer lists every pair of them, lower ID first, sorted by the first ID.

A single mislabelled question can add or drop a user and change many pairs at once. Hidden evaluation was unavailable, so I could not score the result.
